# OpenSRE: Open-Source AI Agent for SRE and Incident Resolution

The video features OpenSRE, an open source framework to create reliability engineering AI (SRE) agents. The agent investigates CI/CD faults and production alerts, crosses logs and metrics, maskes sensitive data and proposes correction. Shows the flow in five steps, integrations and ways to deploy.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on October 7, 2026 (8 min 3 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BTTHq4W56KQ

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The Problem

The AI already writes code in seconds, but when the CI/CD mat fails, this speed runs into slow manual processes [00:00]. In an incident, the clues are scattered: confusing logs, panels of metrics that do not talk, outdated runbooks and long conversations in messages [00:22]. With a short deadline, people click on "rerun" and hope for the error to disappear [00:43]. Or the main branch locks, waiting for the only senior engineer who has the context [01:03].

OpenSRE is an open source framework designed to act as an AI-driven SRE (site reliability engineer) agent [01:03]. It is a toolbox to investigate infrastructure and CI/CD failures [01:24].

## Why diagnosing incidents is difficult

In code tasks, agents evolved because they have scale training data, such as SWE-bench, and fast local feedback cycles [02:05]. In production incidents, faults are distributed and logs are noisy [02:27]. There was no equivalent to SWE-bench for incident response, nor a standardized environment for training AI in real infrastructure problems [02:27].

## What OpenSRE is

According to the video, OpenSRE is not a chatbot where code is pasted: it is a learning environment by reinforcement and a framework [02:49]. He reads the flaw, proposes correction in a pull request and runs on the team's own infrastructure [02:49]. The agent starts acting when the build fails: pulls the logs and tests hypotheses, often before a person opens the pipeline panel [03:09]. The video cites over 11,400 stars in GitHub and over 1,700 forks [03:09].

## How the agent works

The flow has five steps from the alert [03:52]:

1. It seeks the context: the owner of the service, what changed recently and the logs [03:52].
2. Masks sensitive data [03:52].
3. Use the tools and reason about hypotheses, crossing the systems [03:52].
4. Write the answer, with conclusions based on the evidence you read [04:14].
5. Post a summary on the channel where the team already talks [04:14].

The framework accepts various modes of use [04:14]:

- an interactive shell to explain the problem by talking [04:34];
- the headless mode in a continuous integration script [04:34];
- the Python API, within the internal services of the company [04:34];
- a bot in Slack [04:34].

## Integration and security

OpenSRE comes with more than 60 integrations [04:55]. In AI, accept Anthropic, OpenAI or local models with Ollama [05:17]. It connects to observability tools such as Datadog and Grafana, Kubernetes and AWS, banks such as Postgres and Redis, and sends the report to Slack or Discord [05:17]. Thus, the agent investigates with the same tools that an engineer would use [05:39].

To reduce the risk of such access, the agent hides information such as pod names, clusters and account IDs before sending data to an external LLM [05:39]. According to the video, it restores this data only at the time of showing the answer [06:00].

## Implementation

The video describes three paths [06:21]:

- OpenSRE Cloud, a managed gateway [06:21];
- the agent embedded in server images in the team's own cloud [06:21];
- a Dockerfile, to run in container on AWS, Railway or Vercel [06:42].

The installation by script takes about 2 minutes [06:42]. In the first execution, a hosted model is activated for testing, without requiring LLM API key [07:04].

## Final reflection

The video asks how long it's been developing waiting for someone to find out why the main branch is red [07:04]. The proposal of open SRE agents is to remove the engineer from this manual and repetitive work [07:25].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does OpenSRE send sensitive data to LLM?

According to the video, no: it masks pod names, clusters and account IDs before sending data to an external LLM [05:39].

### Do I need API key to test?

Nope. In the first execution, a hosted model is activated for testing [07:04].

### Can I run OpenSRE with a local template?

Yeah. In addition to Anthropic and OpenAI, he accepts local models with Ollama [05:17].

## About the video

In this video, we present the **OpenSRE**, an open-source framework designed to build and execute AI agents focused on Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and incident automation in production environments.

Learn how OpenSRE correlates recent logs, metrics, strokes and deployments, diagnoses real-time failures, and investigates the root cause of problems directly in your own infrastructure.

🎯 **What will you see in this video:**
• **What OpenSRE is**: The open-source toolkit for the era of AI agents.
• **Diagnosis of Incidents**: As the agent analyzes alerts, tests hypotheses and identifies the root cause based on evidence.
• **CI/CD automation**: Automatic pipeline failure diagnosis and automatic pull requests opening with GitHub fixes.
• **Safety and Masking**: Protection of sensitive data and reversible writing of infrastructure identifiers before calls to LLMs.
• **Integration Ecosystem**: Native support for more than 60 tools (Graphana, Datadog, Kubernetes, AWS, Slack, PagerDuty and more).
